name: AN-M65 1,000 lb general-purpose bomb
blurb: The bomb every Allied strike loadout carries. Its model is generated from the Navy's own 1947 ordnance pamphlet.
history:
The AN-M65 was the standard American 1,000-pound general-purpose bomb of the Second World War, used by both the Army Air Forces and the Navy (the AN prefix marks an Army-Navy standard). About half its weight was high explosive, Amatol or TNT, in a thin steel case with an ogival nose, a boat-tailed aft end and a box-type tail. It was hung by two lugs fourteen inches apart and fuzed at the nose and tail.

The bombs were painted olive drab with yellow bands marking the high-explosive filler. Carrier fighters such as the F6F Hellcat carried it under the wing and on the centerline against ships, bridges and airfields in the Pacific.

sources.title: OP 1664, U.S. Explosive Ordnance (Bureau of Ordnance, 1947)
